result.title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
result.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures. Code and provenance verified artifacts: https://github.com/ClevixLab/training-state-equivalence
result.summary: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues. On fresh runs of a one-layer transformer learning modular addition, response to a weight-decay pulse is highly reproducible relative to between-checkpoint differences (rho_state = 0.934 at 500 steps), establishing the target as measurable. Fifteen descriptors of weight spectra, representation geometry and optimiser geometry carry within-run response-relevant information beyond weight norm and loss on a development dataset, predicting held-out response deviation across seed blocks. But their apparent 16.1% advantage at matching checkpoints by future response does not separate from a conditional placebo preserving each descriptor's fitted dependence on the conventional observables, and a calibrated positive control makes simple insensitivity an unlikely explanation. Information a decoder can extract need not be organised in the pairwise geometry that similarity judgments require.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用单层 transformer 学习模加法的多次重跑，操作化定义「训练状态等价」为对训练扰动的响应一致性，并检验权重谱、表示几何与优化器几何等 15 类描述符是否能在权重范数和损失之外预测该响应偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其条件安慰剂与校准正控制的评估设计可供核查，用于检验 latent 状态相似度是否真正反映内容而非可解码信息；「可解码信息不必然组织在成对几何中」也可能提示 LVR 中 latent 相似度比较的效度问题，但迁移属推测。
